question: Will Shri Thanedar be the Democratic Nominee for MI-13?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins the nomination for the Democratic Party to contest the MI-13 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The Democratic primary will take place on August 4, 2026.

If no nominee is announced by November 3, 2026, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democrat sources, including https://democrats.org/.

Any replacement of the nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

evidence.publisher: Detroit Free Press, Clara Hendrickson (republished by AOL)
evidence.excerpt: McKinney had about $264,000 cash on hand to Thanedar's nearly $4.7 million, according to their July campaign finance reports. Waters and Democrat John Goci were disqualified for submitting insufficient voter signatures. Thanedar won 28% in the crowded 2022 congressional primary and 55% in the 2024 primary.

U.S. Rep. Summer Lee endorsed state Rep. Donavan McKinney on Monday in his bid to unseat U.S. Rep. Shri Thanedar. Lee is the first member of the Congressional Black Caucus to endorse a candidate in the race and the second sitting member of Congress to back McKinney, joining Rashida Tlaib. This year's primary is a one-on-one contest after two other Democratic candidates were disqualified.

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, Democratic Whip Katherine Clark, and House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar endorsed Shri Thanedar for re-election in Michigan's 13th Congressional District. Their joint statement praised his constituent service, efforts to lower family costs and opposition to President Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans.

Thanedar gave his campaign $800,000 in June and outraised McKinney last quarter, although his campaign carries his personal loans as debt. Two-thirds of the money Thanedar raised in the quarter came through AIPAC bundlers, according to his latest FEC filing. The campaign reported more than $630,000 in investment-income losses during the quarter.

evidence.publisher: Justice Democrats (dated email preserved by Archive of Political Emails)
evidence.excerpt: A Justice Democrats email reported a new Data for Progress poll showing Thanedar leading McKinney 46% to 42%. The email also described a separate result after respondents were shown candidate biographies, with McKinney at 48% and Thanedar at 41%. Justice Democrats stated that it was supporting McKinney.
